_comment: Relationships a parser cannot infer, written by whoever made the change. Merged by /opt/graphify/semantic_links.py; see .claude/project_rules.md section 4. Endpoints must resolve to exactly one graph node — run the merge and read its output, it names anything that does not.

edges.note: EXEC-1. Gate.io publishes order and trade updates on independent channels, so a fill can be the first message naming a fired conditional order. The fill path reconciles the venue identity before emitting, instead of producing an event Order.apply refuses and the engine swallows.

EXEC-1 regression. Eleven scenarios, nine failing against the previous implementation: fill before any order message, several fills, duplicate replay, unreconcilable identity, reconnect and restart across the transition.

The dual identity: the venue arms an order under one id and creates another when it fires. Both are kept, because the armed id is what still addresses the price order after a restart. Undocumented anywhere until the graph showed this symbol had no documentation edge.

seam-07 / SEAM-02. Asserts the package defines the conversion exactly once by walking the tree. A binary-float copy in data.py disagreed by 64 ns on millisecond timestamps, so one venue instant became two values depending on which path carried it.

seam-08. The factory registers one owner per client and a cached transport that has been closed is rebuilt, because closing it naively would hand a closed client to the next trading node in the process.
The execution path and the data path must agree about the same venue instant; both resolve to one function object so they cannot drift apart again.
A fill whose identity cannot be reconciled inline is routed through reconciliation with an error naming both ids, rather than emitted as an event the platform will refuse and drop.
